There is no possible way I'd pay $20+ for games like this. Cartridges are a terrible idea, and there are good reasons nearly all of the console industry has moved away from them. Such a system may find traction in a very small niche community, but I don't think it will sell very well. Particularly considering the Hyperkin Retron 5 is already available, and plays games from 10 different consoles at the same price point they're aiming for.

The age that this is trying to emulate has already come and gone. Nothing can bring it back in quite the same way. It will always be a poor imitation, because we're living in 2016, not 1982. Part of what defined the retro gaming experience was the culture and time that it existed in. You can't slap together a cartridge based console and expect it to be the same thing. It doesn't make any sense in context in the present day. When we played those old consoles and games originally, they were on the bleeding edge of technology, culture, and creativity.

That's not to say you can't make a great retro-styled game today, but the great new-retro games all have some new spin or refinement that's relevant today. Now maybe there will be games like that on this machine, but does playing it on a cartridge really make it better? Is there any reason to play it on this machine rather than on a PC? If it's an authentic retro game on a retro console with a place in history, that's worth something to me. I only recently got an Atari, but the history behind it and the games is part of the experience. I'm connecting with the past. But playing a game on obsolete hardware manufactured in 2016 with no history behind it seems empty to me. Anyone who expects to pick up a new release for this thing and have the same feeling they did when they got a new NES game in 1988 is in for a disappointment. That's a frustrating thing that we have a hard time accepting, because nowadays we can buy just about anything, but we can't buy that feeling back.
